solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Child facing stern jaw (that of dominie?)

indicators.note: one piece facing another sits right up against it, so the two are joined side by side

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for child
the stern of a ship is aft

explanation.surface: A child confronting a schoolmaster with a severe set of the jaw.
explanation.walkthrough: A dominie is a Scottish schoolmaster, which is the hint that a Scots word for jaw is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaft is a Scots and northern dialect word for the jaw or jawbone, hence the Scottish teacher.

clue.text: Cut so arranged round picnic basket, good for outside party!

indicators.note: going round something means enclosing it on both sides
letters that are arranged are put into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
a hamper is a lidded basket for a picnic

explanation.surface: A cut of meat wrapped round the picnic basket makes a fine treat for an outdoor party.
explanation.walkthrough: Champerty is an outsider funding someone's lawsuit for a share of the winnings; the bloggers queried 'good', but the arrangement certainly benefits the outside party.
explanation.definitionFit: Champertous describes a deal in which a third party backs litigation in return for a cut of any damages.

clue.text: Gang member in murder overlooked by CID?

indicators.note: what is overlooked is missed out, so those letters are left out

parts.note: homicide is the killing of a person
taken as written, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A gang member mixed up in a killing that the detectives failed to spot.
explanation.walkthrough: CID, the Criminal Investigation Department, fits the crime story perfectly, which disguises that it is simply three letters to drop.
explanation.definitionFit: Homie is US slang for a fellow member of one's gang or neighbourhood crew.

clue.text: Bangle craft entered by man (not amateur

indicators.note: a word entered by another has that other placed inside it

parts.note: craft in the sense of skill

indicators.note: not means that this letter is left out of the word before it

parts.note: a man is a male
A is a standard abbreviation for amateur

explanation.surface: An ornament made by a craftsman who is a professional, not an amateur.
explanation.walkthrough: The closing bracket is missing in the source text. The shortened man goes between the second and third letters of the craft word.
explanation.definitionFit: An armlet is a band or bracelet worn round the arm, the same sort of ornament as a bangle.

clue.text: A variety of corn coming up in hardy perennials

definitions.note: plural definition for the genus name

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
millet is a cereal grass grown for grain

explanation.surface: A type of grain sprouting among the tough plants in a border.
explanation.definitionFit: Tellima is a genus of hardy perennial plants of the saxifrage family, grown for ground cover.

clue.text: Nurse, adult one going into health ministry for love

indicators.note: one letter goes into the word in place of another named after the word for

parts.note: A is the film certificate for adult
MOH is the Ministry of Health
a is one, the indefinite article
love is nil, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A grown-up nurse joins the health ministry because she loves the work.
explanation.walkthrough: In the ministry abbreviation the letter for love is swapped for the letter for one, and the adult letter goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: An amah is a children's nurse or maidservant in East and South Asia.

clue.text: Musical coming up, played non-part in the wings, totally dumb

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the letters run upwards
being in the wings means standing just inside the edges, so this goes inside the other part
something played about with is moved round into another order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
Gigi is the Lerner and Loewe film musical

explanation.surface: A musical revival where an actor without a role waits offstage, utterly silent.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre words disguise the mechanics: the reversed musical sits just inside the first letter of the jumbled fodder, as an actor in the wings stands just inside the stage edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig-ignorant is a colloquial term for extremely ignorant or stupid, which is what totally dumb means.

clue.text: Matador from Spain, notice, welcomed by that country but not at home

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: something welcomed by another is taken inside it
not means the following phrase's letters are left out

parts.note: the country just named
someone at home is in
an ad is a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: A Spanish bullfighter whose poster is admired in Spain, though he is away from home.
explanation.walkthrough: Spain is used twice: once for its car code, then as the country to be shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Espada, Spanish for sword, is a name for the matador who kills the bull with a sword.

clue.text: Passing middle of week with…

indicators.note: the middle of a word is just its central letters

parts.note: the two central letters of the word
the ellipsis carries on into the next clue, whose opening words about taking in drinks supply laps, as a cat laps milk

explanation.surface: Time passing in the middle of the week, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The two clues are read as one sentence: the drinks taken in go inside the middle of week.
explanation.definitionFit: To elapse is for time to pass, so passing is its participle used as a noun.

clue.text: …Intake of drinks, half slothful

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, so the second four letters are dropped

parts.note: sluggish means lazy and slow

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue: knocking back drinks makes one half lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening ellipsis links this to the previous clue, which borrows its first words.
explanation.definitionFit: A slug is a large swallow of spirits, a single gulp taken in.

clue.text: Pressure on oil disrupted the States — hairy

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown into disorder

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
the United States

explanation.surface: Pressure on oil supplies has shaken America, and things are getting hairy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilous is a botanical and zoological word for covered with hair, from Latin pilus.

clue.text: Entrails for student examining Mediterranean fish

indicators.note: the entrails are the insides, so the answer lies inside these words

parts.note: the letters run across the junction of the two words

explanation.surface: A biology student examines the guts of a fish from the Med.
explanation.walkthrough: Entrails looks like part of the dissection scene; it signals the inner letters of the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The dentex is a large sea bream of the Mediterranean, named for its prominent teeth.

clue.text: Pair of strays wandering round France, showing off creativity?

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it
letters that are wandering drift out of their order

parts.note: two lots of the word for a stray, the letters to be rearranged
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: Two stray animals roaming France, displaying their imaginative side.
explanation.walkthrough: Each half of the answer is one stray rearranged, with the country letter between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Artsy-fartsy is a derisive term for pretentiously arty, flaunting creative or cultural pretensions.

clue.text: Decorator of old mounts, Jack maybe frames one left border in reverse

indicators.note: a frame goes round a picture, so this word goes round the rest

parts.note: Little Jack Horner of the nursery rhyme

indicators.note: in reverse means read from the end back to the start

parts.note: Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for left
a limes is a boundary, especially a fortified frontier of the Roman Empire

explanation.surface: A decorator mounts pictures for Jack, framing one with its left border reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: Mounts suggests framing pictures but means horses. The border word is the answer to 25 down.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-milliner was a tradesman who supplied the decorative trimmings for horses' harness and saddlery.

clue.text: Mum holds festive occasion back for wine (sweet)

indicators.note: something that holds another has it inside

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read the other way

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration

explanation.surface: Mother brings back sweet wine from a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaga is a sweet fortified wine from the area around the Spanish city of that name.

clue.text: Have a fag? Och aye, not easily cutting b– leaves!

indicators.note: when something leaves it goes away, so this letter is dropped

parts.note: a blunt blade does not cut easily
the dashed b is the letter itself, posing as a bleeped-out swear word

explanation.surface: A Scot offered a cigarette swears at the blunt knife hacking at tobacco leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Och aye flags Scots; a fag is British slang for a cigarette. b– looks like a censored oath and leaves looks like tobacco, but both are mechanics.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunt is a Scots verb meaning to smoke a pipe or cigarette, so it fits a Scottish invitation to smoke.

clue.text: Spleen on being spurned by poet

indicators.note: what is spurned is rejected, so these letters are thrown out of the other word

parts.note: John Milton, author of Paradise Lost
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone venting their bile after a poet rejects them.
explanation.walkthrough: Spleen invites the bad-temper sense; here it is the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Milt is an old word for the spleen as well as for fish roe.

clue.text: Sciatica: after hospital I set about activity

indicators.note: about means around, enclosing the next piece
after says which piece comes later in the line-up

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
taken as written
to set something down is to put it
go as in energy or bustle

explanation.surface: A patient explains that after leaving hospital they took up exercise for their back pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Hip-gout is an old name for sciatica, pain running from the hip down the leg.

clue.text: Pig seen excitedly gobbling last of swill — these included?

definitions.text: Pig seen excitedly gobbling last of swill — these included?

indicators.note: something done excitedly is done in a jumbled, frantic way
gobbling means taking in, adding the extra letter to the fodder before mixing

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pig spotted wolfing down the dregs of its swill, kitchen scraps among them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: pig swill is made of kitchen scraps, vegetable skins among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Peelings are the discarded skins of fruit and vegetables, a staple of the scraps fed to pigs.

clue.text: Nauseous on horseback, turning back essential

indicators.note: turning back means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a rider is up on the horse
key means crucial or essential

explanation.surface: Feeling sick on a horse, a rider turns back, which is vital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pukey is an informal adjective for feeling sick, as if about to vomit.

clue.text: …Ayseed surrounded by litter? Improvements called for

indicators.note: something surrounded by another sits inside it

parts.note: a litter of young dogs
hayseed is a hick; dropping the H as a Cockney would leaves the rest

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin stuck among the rubbish calls for things to get better.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue had an apostrophe, 'Ayseed, marking the dropped H; this copy shows an ellipsis. A hayseed is a rustic, as is a hick.
explanation.definitionFit: Pick-ups are recoveries or improvements, as when trade or the economy picks up.

clue.text: Tailless chicken, odd family

parts.note: rum means strange, an old British colloquialism
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A strange tailless hen with an equally peculiar family.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumkin is a domestic fowl without a tail, a breed lacking the rump.

clue.text: One comes up in line for closing number

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: a file is a line of people one behind another

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading the letters bottom to top

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A chorus line member steps up for the show's last song.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the last piece of a performance, the closing number of a show.

clue.text: Fidgety yapper you need to settle in advance

indicators.note: something fidgety cannot keep still, so its letters move around

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A restless barking dog has to be settled down ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Settle looks like calming the dog; it is settling a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepay is to pay a bill or charge before receiving the goods or service.

clue.text: Pages from book disturbed sleep

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book

indicators.note: something disturbed is knocked out of its proper order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Turning the pages of a book kept someone from sleeping.
explanation.walkthrough: Pages reads as the leaves of the book but is a verb: calling someone on a pager.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleep someone is to summon them by pager, which is exactly what paging them means.

clue.text: Note this ulcer, new, getting worse? An eruption possibly

indicators.note: a condition getting worse is in a mess, so these letters are jumbled
possibly says the phrase is one possible arrangement of the letters, not the only one

parts.note: the letters that the jumbled answer and extras make up
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A doctor notes a fresh ulcer that seems to be getting worse, perhaps a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a compound anagram: the answer plus the note and new letters is a jumble of the last two words, so remove those letters from that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupia is a skin condition with crusted ulcers, seen in late syphilis, so it is an ulcerous eruption.

clue.text: Lichens, endless danger on part of Parthenon?

definitions.note: plural definition for the genus name

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a rock is a hazard to shipping, figuratively a danger
the cella is the inner chamber of a classical temple

explanation.surface: Lichen growing endlessly on the ruins of the Parthenon is a threat to it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the Parthenon as an example: any classical temple has a cella.
explanation.definitionFit: Roccella is a genus of lichens, the source of the dye orchil, so it covers several lichens.

clue.text: …Is situated round edge of imperium?

indicators.note: round means surrounding the next piece

parts.note: something situated somewhere lies there

indicators.note: an edge is an end, so only an outermost letter is taken

parts.note: the letter at one edge of the word

explanation.surface: The ellipsis stands for the answer: this lies round the edge of an empire.
explanation.walkthrough: As a commenter explained, the ellipsis is a blank for the answer, so the whole clue reads as a sentence defining it and also as the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Limes, Latin for boundary, was the fortified frontier round the edge of the Roman Empire.

clue.text: Huntsman reset net in wild moor

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
something reset is put in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged as the outer piece

indicators.note: wild letters are out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged as the inner piece

explanation.surface: A huntsman setting a net again out on the open moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: Montero is Spanish for a hunter; in English it is a huntsman, also his round cap with flaps.

clue.text: What'll protect clothing in rumpus room row?

definitions.text: What'll protect clothing in rumpus room
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a child's pinafore, in American usage
second meaning: one of a series of rows set one above another

explanation.surface: A fight in a playroom, and something to keep the children's clothes clean.
explanation.walkthrough: Rumpus room is an American term for a games or playroom, hinting at the US sense of a pinafore. Row looks like a quarrel to match the rumpus, but it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is both a child's pinafore in US usage and one of several rows rising in steps.

clue.text: See me going through Calvados, a drink with a bit of richness in

indicators.note: with this inside means the letter goes into the other piece

parts.note: one as in having one, a drink

indicators.note: a bit of a word means just one letter, here the first

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A tourist in Normandy samples the local brandy, finding it rich.
explanation.walkthrough: Calvados reads as the apple brandy but is the Normandy department the river runs through, and the drink in the clue is something else.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orne is a river of Normandy flowing through the department of Calvados to the sea near Caen.

clue.text: Scots guard — or Welsh, English and Irish

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for Welsh
E is the abbreviation for English
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A list of the British Army's national regiments: Scots Guards, Welsh, English and Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: Scots Guards and Welsh and Irish Guards are real regiments, so the clue reads as a roll-call; here guard is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Weir, or wear, is a Scots verb meaning to guard or protect, as in herding animals.

clue.text: Chef alienating company with almost uncooked slimy veg

indicators.note: alienating means driving away, so these letters go

parts.note: a chef is a cook
CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: raw food is not cooked

explanation.surface: A cook upsets the diners by serving half-raw, slippery vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: A commenter noted that the vegetable turns slimy when cooked, which is what makes it good for thickening gumbo.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra, also called ladies' fingers, is a pod vegetable whose mucilage gives it a slimy texture.

clue.text: Arab wearing unadulterated set of ornaments

indicators.note: someone wearing something has it on, so here this word is put on around it

parts.note: pure means not mixed with anything
AR is the abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

explanation.surface: A sheikh wearing genuine jewels in a matching set.
explanation.definitionFit: A parure is a matching set of jewels or ornaments, such as a necklace, earrings and brooch.

clue.text: Pile-ups with 'Annie L' being played, whereon chanter's deployed (13, two words)

indicators.note: a tune being played is worked through, and these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: the first set of letters to be rearranged
the second set of letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Crashes on the road while a song called Annie L plays, with someone singing along.
explanation.walkthrough: Chanter looks like a singer, but it is the pipe on which a bagpipe player fingers the melody.
explanation.definitionFit: Uilleann pipes, the Irish bagpipes, have a chanter, the fingered melody pipe, like other bagpipes.

clue.text: Contemptuous, as always featured in channel that's not main one

indicators.note: something featured in another appears inside it

parts.note: a sny or snye is a side channel of a river
e'er is the poetic short form of ever

explanation.surface: A dismissive presenter, always appearing on some minor television channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Channel suggests television, but it is a stream branching off a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneery is an informal adjective for scornful, inclined to sneer at others.

clue.text: Crybaby? Only part of class is sympathetic

indicators.note: only part of these words is used, the answer tucked inside them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the first word through the second into the third

explanation.surface: A classroom crybaby, but only some of the class feel sorry for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sissy is a timid or cowardly person, and a crybaby is a typical example, hence the question mark.
